clue.text: Celebrity edges king out

indicators.note: out tells us the king is put out of the word for edges

parts.note: the frame of a picture is its edges or border
R is the abbreviation for king (Latin rex)

explanation.surface: A famous figure gently nudges a monarch from the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrity and renown are synonyms for being widely known.

clue.text: Looking up recent file, cafeteria incorporates improved frontage

indicators.note: Looking up says the hidden letters are read backwards, upward in a down clue
the clue words incorporate, or contain, the letters wanted within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone browsing a recent file notes that the cafeteria has had its shopfront smartened up.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'incorporates' as part of the definition; it is the signal that the letters sit inside 'recent file, cafeteria', leaving 'improved frontage' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic operation to the face, or a renovation of a building's front, both give an improved frontage.

clue.text: Press and TV nonsense upset referee

parts.note: the press and television together are the media

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word for nonsense upside down, reading it upwards

parts.note: rot is nonsense

explanation.surface: Rubbish in the newspapers and on television has annoyed a match official.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee is someone who arbitrates between parties, synonym for a go-between who settles disputes.

clue.text: Moderate OK about cheers meeting Left's fibs

parts.note: fair means moderate, middling

indicators.note: about says the word for OK goes around the following letters

parts.note: yes means OK, agreed

indicators.note: meeting puts the cheers word right next to the left letter

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
L is the abbreviation for left; the 's reads as 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition

explanation.surface: A middling approval of a toast, combined with left-wing untruths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderate' looks like a verb but is an adjective here; 'about' wraps the word for OK round both cheers and the left letter, which 'meeting' joins together.
explanation.definitionFit: Fanciful stories that are untrue are lies, so the phrase is a gentle idiom for fibs.

clue.text: Together making a wish

parts.note: to long for something is to wish for it

explanation.surface: Two people make a wish as one.
explanation.definitionFit: To come with someone is to go in company, so the adverb is a synonym for together.

clue.text: 'Rays' created by Academician an idiot restored

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

indicators.note: restored means the letters of the phrase are put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: Something called 'Rays' was produced by an artist, with a fool brought back to life.
explanation.definitionFit: Energy emitted as waves or particles is described as rays, a synonym for emitted radiant energy.

clue.text: Dramatic crash makes this half-cut junior give applause

indicators.note: half-cut asks for only the first half of the word this

parts.note: a junior is one under another in rank
to clap is to give applause

explanation.surface: A tipsy young person loudly applauds a dramatic noise.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-cut is British slang for drunk, but here it trims 'this' to its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden loud peal heard in a storm is a dramatic crash.

clue.text: Fondness shown by Simba not on?

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the word on from the title

parts.note: Simba is the lion cub hero of Disney's The Lion King

explanation.surface: A query about whether the lion cub Simba is loved or not.
explanation.definitionFit: A fondness for something is a taste or preference, a synonym.

clue.text: Calls tailors

definitions.meaning: to call someone something is to give them a name or title
tailors here is a verb: shapes or designs something to fit, as with a cut or fashion

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to designate by a title and to design or fashion something to a particular cut.

clue.text: Poem by Conservative concealed message

indicators.note: by puts the conservative letter beside the poem

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A Tory politician's verse hides a secret meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A cipher system hides meaning, so a concealed message is written in one.

clue.text: Desperately giving up the Boxing Day diet?

definitions.meaning: abrupt total withdrawal from an addiction, with its unpleasant symptoms
the day after Christmas, leftovers of the roast bird are eaten chilled

explanation.surface: Someone on Boxing Day despairingly abandons their healthy eating plan.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxing Day is 26 December, a British holiday when Christmas leftovers are eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names sudden, total abstinence from a drug, and literally the chilled leftover festive bird.

clue.text: First thing taken from church roof in middle of night

parts.note: lead sheeting is notoriously stolen from church roofs

indicators.note: middle of asks for the central letter of the word night

explanation.surface: Thieves strip a church roof in the dead of night.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in front of all others, top-ranked, is the same as being first.

clue.text: Killer in cult that is infiltrated by detectives

parts.note: a sect is a religious cult

indicators.note: infiltrated by says the detectives get inside the abbreviation for that is

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

explanation.surface: Undercover detectives get inside a murderous cult.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical spray for bugs is a killer of pests, so killer is a general term for it.

clue.text: Firm for consumers with depression cutting alcohol

indicators.note: cutting means the dent goes into the middle of the drink

parts.note: ale is an alcoholic drink
a dent is a small depression in a surface

explanation.surface: A company targeting shoppers who are feeling low and cutting back on drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian phrase for pasta cooked to be firm to the bite, so firm for those eating it.

clue.text: Pedestrian ready for a fight?

parts.note: a walker who is armed for battle: an infantryman, who marches on foot

explanation.surface: A walker is spoiling for a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: An infantryman fights on foot, so he is literally a pedestrian ready for combat.

clue.text: Demolished hot meal, so becoming obnoxious

indicators.note: demolished means knocked down and rebuilt, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wolfing down a hot dinner makes someone unpleasant company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demolished' looks like eating up a meal, but it signals rearranging the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repulsive and hateful is obnoxious, a close synonym.

clue.text: Drawing competition — little craft used in encounter?

definitions.meaning: a contest of pulling a rope, drawing meaning pulling, not sketching
a small towing boat employed in battle, read literally

explanation.surface: An art contest, and a tiny vessel deployed in a clash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' suggests art; here it means pulling a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: The rope-pulling team contest is a pulling competition, and literally a small boat of battle.

clue.text: Pretentious cafe — fed excitedly, with time to tuck in

indicators.note: to tuck in is to put inside, so the time letter goes into the mixed letters
excitedly means the letters of the two words are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A snooty café where diners are fed with gusto and given time to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tuck in' suggests eating, but after 'excitedly' makes AFFECED it puts the time letter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy and artificial behaviour is pretentious, a synonym.

clue.text: Keep on depressing remote journey to Calais, unconventionally?

definitions.meaning: flick through TV stations by pressing the buttons of a remote control repeatedly
riding a wave across the stretch of sea between England and France

explanation.surface: Someone keeps glumly pressing the remote, dreaming of an odd trip to France.
explanation.walkthrough: Calais is the French port across the English Channel from Dover.
explanation.definitionFit: Zapping between TV stations is the idiom, and literally riding a surfboard over the English sea.

clue.text: Disorderly scrap over touching pursuit

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the scrap above the game

parts.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth
tag is the playground chasing game in which you touch the other player

explanation.surface: An unruly scuffle breaks out over a game of chase.
explanation.definitionFit: Motley, untidy and unorganised describes a disorderly group.

clue.text: Something dug up and stored in depot at Oldham

indicators.note: stored in means the letters are kept inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Something unearthed is kept in a warehouse in Oldham.
explanation.walkthrough: Oldham is a town near Manchester in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Tubers are harvested from the soil, so this vegetable is an example of something dug up.

clue.text: Bar has rum — boil, stirring, to infuse

indicators.note: to infuse means the stirred letters are steeped inside the others
rum is old British slang for odd, so the letters are oddly arranged
stirring mixes up the letters of the word boil

explanation.surface: A drinks bar heats rum and stirs it into a hot infusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' (old slang for odd) gives ASH and 'stirring' gives BOLI, which 'to infuse' steeps inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar something is to prohibit it, to do away with it by law.

clue.text: Apparently 3 beg

definitions.meaning: 3-across is fairy tales; split in two, the word suggests a mischievous sprite plus traditional stories
to beg is to entreat or plead

explanation.definitionFit: To beg someone is to plead earnestly, a synonym; split, it reads as folklore of goblins.

clue.text: More slippery French here looking down on the Queen

indicators.note: looking down on in a down clue places the French word above the queen

parts.note: ici is French for here
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A slippery French local looks down on the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Roads with more frost are slicker, so the comparative means more slippery.

clue.text: Bittersweet hybrid of citric mango with no name

indicators.note: a hybrid mixes things, so the letters of the fruit words are crossed into a new order
with no says one letter of the fodder is lost

explanation.surface: A cross between citrus and mango, minus its label, tastes bittersweet.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove N from CITRIC MANGO and rearrange the remaining ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Mixing tragedy and comedy gives a work that is both sad and funny, bittersweet.

clue.text: Trap wasp — oddly, rotating fly-killer could do this

indicators.note: rotating turns the chosen letters round to read backwards
oddly picks the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: Instructions for catching a wasp: a spinning bug-killer might manage it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fly-swatter's job is to strike a fly sharply, so that is what it could do.

clue.text: Duo's accompanist won't enjoy playing this

definitions.text: Duo's accompanist won't enjoy playing this

parts.words: Duo's accompanist won't enjoy playing this
parts.note: a third person tagging along with a courting couple is said to play a fruit's part, an unwelcome role

explanation.surface: A pianist accompanying a musical duo dislikes a particular piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom 'play gooseberry' means to be the unwanted third person with a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit names the role of an unwanted chaperone to a pair of lovers, which nobody enjoys.

clue.text: Took steps, seeing team's leader standing beside bar

indicators.note: standing beside places the rod after the leading letter
the team's leader is its first letter

parts.note: a rod is a bar

explanation.surface: The captain walks over to stand by the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of tread means walked, so it means took steps.
